text:
maria: Quick follow-up to the kernel-autotune RFC — we need to decide how aggressive the runtime's feedback loop should be between observed metrics (p95 token latency, kv cache hit rate, and token-efficiency) and adjustments to prefill depth / bucket boundaries. I sketched a control loop that nudges prefill_depth and bucket_threshold every minute using a rolling window. Safety question: how do we avoid oscillations and wasted prefill compute when traffic is spiky? :thinking:

ajay: Strong +1 on adding hysteresis and clamping. My gut: only allow a single parameter change per minute, and cap magnitude (e.g. +/- 10% per change). Also require a minimum sample size (n_requests >= 100) before any change.

lucas: We should use a composite objective: latency p95 + token-efficiency penalty (wasted prefill tokens * cost). That will prevent tuning from optimizing latency at huge cost. Also use median and 95th percentiles on separate windows and ignore top/bottom 1% outliers to avoid reacting to noise.

sara: Experiment suggestion: rollout the auto-adjuster to a small fleet as a canary. Expose an /admin/heuristics endpoint that returns the active knobs per worker and a timeline of changes so SRE/product can audit. For canary, add an opt-out tag for a subset of customers.

maria: Good point about cost. Lucas, can you propose a simple scoring function we can compute cheaply in the runtime? We need something that fits in the telemetry pipeline (1s aggregation).

lucas: Proposal (simple): score = alpha * (p95_ms / target_p95_ms) + beta * (wasted_tokens / tokens_served). alpha, beta small floats. Tune alpha vs beta offline with historical traces. That keeps math cheap.

ajay: Also: add a cooldown window after an eviction/pre-fill change where we don't auto-adjust again (e.g. 5 min). Eviction churn is the killer.

oliver: From kernel selection side: prefer non-blocking prefetch / background warmup where possible. If a worker starts background prefill of KV for long-seq profiles, it should not block short requests; otherwise head-of-line blocking kills p95. Maybe introduce 'prefill_priority' levels so runtime can prefill opportunistically when GPU has spare SM cycles.

maria: I like prefill_priority. We should define 3 levels: 0 (sync prefill, for guaranteed low-latency long requests), 1 (opportunistic background prefill), 2 (deferred/no prefill). Defaults: short-seq clients -> 2, mixed traffic patterns -> 1.

sara: Small ops note: the heuristics code currently lives in runtime core. For safer experiments and easier rollbacks, can we move the decision logic to a sidecar/process that writes decisions to a config API consumed by runtime? That makes canarying and observability simpler.

ajay: Agreed — separate heuristics service with a gRPC read endpoint. Runtime keeps a conservative default locally so it never stalls if heuristics service is unavailable.

lucas: One more: kernel hinting in model metadata. If model manifest includes "prefer_kernel_family": "int8_fused_attn" or "prefill_hint": "safe_small", the heuristics service can bias its choices. Long-term we should standardize these hints in model-ops.

maria: action items: 1) Lucas to draft scoring function and knob ranges (due EOD Wed). 2) Ajay to prototype hysteresis + clamps config (PR). 3) Sara to create canary plan and /admin/heuristics stub. 4) Oliver to spec prefill_priority semantics for kernel layer. I'll sync w/ infra about telemetry windows.

tuning-bot: autotune-run started: model=redwood-v0.9, run_id=run-20240315-42, target_p95=120ms, initial_prefill_depth=32. logs: https://ci.internal/rt-tune/run-20240315-42

maria: tiny UX request: make the /admin/heuristics output human-readable in the console and include last-change reason (metric that triggered it). That will save us 30 min of guesswork in postmortems.

ajay: code snippet for conservative clamp prototype (pseudo):
```
{
  "prefill_depth": clamp(old_prefill * delta, min=8, max=128),
  "bucket_threshold_ms": clamp(old_bucket + step_ms, min=20, max=500)
}
```

sara: test plan: canary for 10% of workers, 2-hour burn-in, compare cost/token and p95 before/after, abort if p95 regresses >5% or cost/token increases >15%.

maria: perfect. I'll file a follow-up RFC comment summarizing this and link the PRs. Thanks all. :handshake:
